law.value: Public Law 119-21 (H.R. 1), § 71119 — added Section 1902(xx) to the Social Security Act
law.detail: Signed July 4, 2025. CMS refers to the law as the "Working Families Tax Cut" legislation. The requirement cannot be waived under a section 1115 demonstration.

law.value: Welfare and Institutions Code § 14005.69, as amended by AB 2161 (Chapter 209, Statutes of 2026)
law.detail: Approved by the Governor September 14, 2026; filed with the Secretary of State September 14, 2026; chaptered September 15, 2026. The section "shall remain operative only as long as Section 1396a(xx) of Title 42 … is operative" and DHCS must adopt regulations by July 1, 2029.

law.value: No sooner than January 1, 2027 (states may implement sooner)
law.detail: California's statute mirrors this: "No sooner than January 1, 2027 … an applicable individual shall demonstrate work or community engagement," and only after DHCS confirms systems are programmed. CMS's interim final rule was issued June 1, 2026 and published June 3, 2026.

law.value: Medicaid enrollees in the ACA adult expansion group, ages 19–64
law.detail: Individuals eligible to enroll or enrolled under the state plan in the adult group described at § 1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(VIII), and certain section 1115 demonstration populations with minimum essential coverage who are 19–64, not pregnant, and not on Medicare.

law.value: 80 hours per month of qualifying activity, or $580 of monthly income
law.detail: $580 = the federal minimum wage of $7.25 per hour × 80 hours.

law.value: congress.gov — H.R. 1 enrolled text, Public Law 119-21
law.detail: CMS summary decks and the Congressional Research Service analysis (CRS R48633) are linked in the Sources page as convenient starting points.

subject.detail: Under 19 is excluded; 65+ is covered by Medicare and other Medi-Cal pathways.

subject.value: MAGI New Adult Group (aid code M1) — ACA adult group, income up to 138% FPL
subject.detail: "The MAGI New Adult Group (i.e. aid code M1), as prescribed in Section 1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(VIII) of the ACA, extends Medicaid eligibility to all adults aged 19 to 64, including those without dependent children and parents with income over 109% but at or below 138% of the federal poverty level."
"Work and community engagement requirements only apply to applicants and members enrolled in Medi-Cal under the MAGI New Adult Group, regardless of immigration status."

"Medi-Cal eligibility is determined at the individual level … All individuals must independently meet the participation criteria; one individual's compliance cannot be used to satisfy another's requirement."

subject.item: Pregnancy, Medicare, or another Medi-Cal group
subject.detail: Pregnant or postpartum individuals, Medicare Part A or B enrollees, and members of the Mandatory Children's, Pregnancy, and Non-MAGI groups are excluded.

excluded.item: Blind or disabled (Social Security Act § 1614 definition)
excluded.detail: Listed as medically frail or otherwise having special medical needs, including "an individual who is blind or disabled, as defined in Section 1382c of Title 42." Also listed in DHCS's own exemption table, which includes substance use disorder, disabling mental disorder, physical/intellectual/developmental disability that significantly impairs activities of daily living, and serious or complex medical conditions.

excluded.item: Parent, guardian, caretaker relative, or family caregiver of a dependent child age 13 or younger
excluded.detail: When there are two parents in the household, both parents are eligible for this exemption.
Parents, guardians, caretaker relatives, and family caregivers (RAISE Family Caregivers Act definition) of a disabled individual of any age.

excluded.item: Caregiver of someone with a chronic or other health condition, disability, or functional limitation
excluded.detail: WIC § 14005.69(b)(2)(F). This is broader than the federal list.

excluded.item: Pregnant or entitled to postpartum medical assistance
excluded.detail: Includes the 12 months after pregnancy ends.
Foster youth or former foster youth under 26.

excluded.item: American Indian, Alaska Native, or California Indian
excluded.detail: Including individuals determined eligible for Indian Health Service.

excluded.item: Veteran with a total disability rating

excluded.detail: "An individual in compliance with the work requirements under the federal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF)."

excluded.item: Household receives CalFresh (SNAP) and is not exempt from the SNAP work requirement
excluded.detail: A member of a household that receives SNAP benefits and is not exempt from a work requirement under the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008.

excluded.item: In a drug or alcohol treatment and rehabilitation program
excluded.detail: As defined in section 2012(h) of Title 7 of the United States Code.

excluded.item: Inmate of a public institution, or released within the last 90 days
excluded.detail: Inmate of a local, state, or federal public institution; or at any point during the three-month period ending on the first day of the month, the individual was an inmate.

excluded.item: Under 19, or enrolled in Medicare Part A or Part B
excluded.value: Deemed to have demonstrated community engagement
excluded.detail: WIC § 14005.69(f)(1)–(2). Also covers individuals described in § 1396a(a)(10)(A)(i)(I)–(VII), i.e. most other mandatory Medicaid pathways.

comply.value: 80 hours or more in the month
comply.detail: California's law: "The individual works no less than 80 hours." DHCS adds that a job includes self-employment, working at least 80 hours a month.

comply.value: 80 hours or more in the month
comply.detail: Vol unpaid or volunteer work. The member notice phrases it as "volunteer, do community service."

comply.value: 80 hours or more in the month
comply.detail: Job training program. California defines "work program" using section 2015(o)(1) of Title 7 (the SNAP work-program definition).

California's definition adds high schools and state-approved high-school-equivalency programs to the federal list (institutions of higher education and career and technical education). The member notice is more generous in plain language: "Go to school at least part time."

comply.value: Any mix totalling 80 hours or more in the month
comply.detail: Students attending less than part time can combine class and school-activity hours with work, community service, or job training.

comply.item: Income test — the practical route for a trader
comply.value: Total monthly income of at least $580 (80 × $7.25 federal minimum wage)
comply.detail: California law (WIC § 14005.69(e)(6)) measures this as "total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods." DHCS policy guidance describes it as "An individual's total gross income for a month must meet or exceed this amount." The member notice says "an income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes) in any month since your last renewal." For fluctuating income, DHCS allows averaging the prior 6 months; the member notice says the same: "People whose hours change frequently or who have seasonal jobs can average at least $580 per month from any source over 6 months."

comply.value: Average monthly income over the preceding 6 months of at least $580
comply.detail: Seasonal worker is defined by section 45R(d)(5)(B) of the Internal Revenue Code. In California this is WIC § 14005.69(e)(7).

hardship.detail: Inpatient hospital services, nursing facility services, intermediate care facility services for individuals with intellectual disabilities, inpatient psychiatric hospital services, or services of similar acuity, including related outpatient care, as determined by HHS — on the individual's request.

hardship.item: Federal emergency or disaster in your county
hardship.detail: A county in which an emergency or disaster was declared by the President under the National Emergencies Act or the Stafford Act.

A county with an unemployment rate at or above the lesser of 8% or 1.5 times the national unemployment rate. This depends on where you live, and DHCS says it will send a separate notice if your county qualifies.

hardship.item: Travel outside your community for medical care
hardship.detail: You or your dependent must travel outside your community for an extended period to receive medical services necessary to treat a serious or complex medical condition not available in your community — on your request.

timing.value: The look-back month — the calendar month immediately preceding the month you apply
timing.detail: If you were not compliant in the look-back month but become compliant in your application month, coverage starts the first day of the month after compliance begins, and earlier months are denied.

timing.value: Any one month between your last determination and your next redetermination
timing.detail: The months do not have to be consecutive. At a six-month renewal, participation in one or more months since the last determination is enough.

timing.value: Every 6 months instead of 12, starting January 2027
timing.detail: Section 71107 of H.R. 1. Tribal members, pregnant members or those in the 12 months postpartum, and children are not subject to the six-month renewal rule.

timing.value: 1 month for the MAGI New Adult Group, 2 months for all other groups
timing.detail: Effective for applications dated January 1, 2027 or later, per DHCS ACWDL 26-07. To get retroactive coverage you must have met the work rule (or qualified for an exemption) in the retroactive month.

noncompliance.value: You get 30 calendar days to show compliance or an exemption
noncompliance.detail: The county must not deny an application for non-compliance until the 30-day period expires. For enrolled members, Medi-Cal continues during the 30 days. The notice must state how to show compliance, how to show an exemption, the deadline, where to send it, the consequences, how to reapply, information about short-term hardship, and your right to a state hearing.

noncompliance.value: The county must consider every other basis of Medi-Cal eligibility before denying
noncompliance.detail: "Before denying the applicable individual's application or disenrolling the individual, the county shall … Determine whether there is any other basis of eligibility for the Medi-Cal program or for another insurance affordability program." WIC § 14005.69(k)(1)(E) and (n).

noncompliance.value: You receive written notice and an opportunity for a state fair hearing
noncompliance.detail: Also: a person is deemed to have received the notice 5 days after the date on it, and self-attestation that a timely notice was not received is good cause for missing the 30-day window.

noncompliance.item: 4. If a county's data sources conflict
noncompliance.value: The county must ask you to confirm before taking any adverse action
noncompliance.detail: WIC § 14005.69(i). This is a protection added by AB 2161 in 2026.

noncompliance.value: Losing Medi-Cal this way also ends your Covered California financial help
noncompliance.detail: DHCS member notice: "If you lose Medi-Cal because you did not meet these rules, you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California. That means you would have to pay the full cost of new health insurance." County policy says the same.

noncompliance.item: 6. You can re-apply at any time
noncompliance.value: Reapplying is allowed, and compliance is re-assessed on the new application
noncompliance.detail: CMS: "Individuals who are disenrolled may reapply at any time and will be assessed for compliance upon reapplication."

ca-implementation.value: County policy letter — the operating manual
ca-implementation.detail: Defines who is subject, the exemption table, the qualifying activities, look-back and renewal timing, the NNC process, and what happens when someone moves into or out of the MAGI New Adult Group. It states on its face that it is "preliminary guidance and is subject to change based on developing federal policy guidance and state legislative changes."

ca-implementation.value: Six-month renewals for the New Adult Group
ca-implementation.detail: Implements § 71107: redeterminations every six months, with work-rule assessment at each full renewal.

ca-implementation.value: The "Dear Medi-Cal Member" notice being mailed now
ca-implementation.detail: Mailed to current New Adult Group members from late August 2026, and included with application materials from October 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026. This is the plain-language version of the same rules quoted throughout this site.

ca-implementation.value: The California statute now on the books
ca-implementation.detail: Amends WIC § 14005.69. Adds a deferral clause: if a change creates a fiscal impact requiring an appropriation that has not been made, DHCS may defer implementing that change and must notify the Legislature and publish the notice on its website.

Published in the Federal Register on June 3, 2026. States must generally implement no later than January 1, 2027; states may offer short-term hardship exceptions; verification happens at application, renewal, and optionally more often.
Sets out the state's work-plan for the work rule, six-month renewals, non-citizen coverage changes, reduced retroactive coverage periods, and cost sharing.

ca-implementation.item: Where to read DHCS's plain-language version
ca-implementation.detail: The member portal referenced in DHCS's text messages and the outreach letter.

state-funded.value: Applies to adults eligible under § 1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(VIII) (the ACA adult group)
state-funded.detail: Federal law conditions eligibility for the federally funded adult group on community engagement.

state-funded.value: Also applies to state-funded Medi-Cal adults meeting the same criteria
state-funded.detail: WIC § 14005.69(b)(1)(B) and DHCS ACWDL 25-30: "Work and community engagement requirements only apply to applicants and members enrolled in Medi-Cal under the MAGI New Adult Group, regardless of immigration status." Federal law did not require California to extend the rule to state-funded adults.

state-funded.value: If you are a permanent resident still inside the five-year bar, your Medi-Cal is state-funded
state-funded.detail: California still provides full-scope Medi-Cal to immigrants regardless of status, and California will still apply the work rule to you. If you have completed the five-year bar, you are federally funded and the rule applies under the federal baseline as well.

pending.detail: DHCS states it is "awaiting additional federal guidance from CMS" on the definition of medically frail, standards for self-attestation, acceptable forms of verification, criteria for exemptions and work activities, and accelerated enrollment.
pending.flag: Pending federal guidance. DHCS has not published final criteria for these items as of 2026-10-18. Whether a given condition qualifies as medically frail is therefore not confirmable from an official source today.

pending.item: Which programs count as a "work program" and what counts as "community service"
pending.detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30 says "DHCS will provide additional guidance of what constitutes a work program in a future letter" and the same for community service.
pending.flag: Pending DHCS guidance. A specific activity cannot be confirmed as qualifying until DHCS issues the follow-up letter.

pending.item: Whether self-attestation alone is enough, and which documents are acceptable
pending.detail: Listed by DHCS among the areas awaiting federal guidance. California statute requires the county to use available reliable data and, "where possible and only when sufficient verification has been submitted," not to require extra information from the applicant.
pending.flag: Pending federal guidance. The exact evidence needed to prove 80 hours is not fixed in an official source yet.
